plan.disposition: Phase Matrix: External LLM Review is 'skip' at small complexity (auto only at medium+); no mini-plan exists at small for a BUG path, so there is no plan artifact to review.

findings.finding: The orphan advisory's top-5 truncation systematically hides the markers that motivated the feature. Measured against the live cache: 22 .orphaned_at markers exist - 14 under plugins/shipwright-*/ (the mirror tree this check explicitly declares out of scope) and 8 under shared/*, including shared/scripts, the exact directory whose reap broke F11. sorted() puts every plugins/... entry before any shared/... entry, and _print_orphan_advisory shows markers[:5]. On the machine where the incident was measured the operator sees five mirror-tree paths and is never told that shared/scripts is flagged.

The advisory prescribes a remedy that cannot clear it, so it becomes permanent noise. update-marketplace.sh Step 3 deletes cache-only files under shared/, so the 8 shared markers clear. But Step 4's sync_dir_from_to has no removal loop, so the 14 plugins/shipwright-*/.orphaned_at markers survive every sync forever - an always-on warning is indistinguishable from a real one.

Catalog X (dead code, justification removed). TRACKED_SUFFIXES and TEXT_SUFFIXES are byte-identical tuples, so file_hash's binary branch is unreachable from walk_tracked_files. The ORIGINAL docstring said so explicitly; the extraction deleted that clause, so a reader sees a live-looking branch with no way to learn it is dead.

sys.path asymmetry: the module under test appends and documents why (ADR-045); the new test insert(0)s. scripts/hooks/ has no __init__.py, so `hooks` resolves as a namespace package whose portion list is built in sys.path order, and three other modules in the same shared/tests root import it. Resolves correctly today only because scripts/hooks/ holds no .py file.

assert "mirrors" not in result is near-vacuous - no code has ever produced a key by that name, so it can only fail if someone adds that exact string literal. If the mirror were later folded into plugins, or keyed `mirror`, this passes.

test_early_return_statuses_carry_the_documented_shape says 'statuses' but exercises only cache_root_absent; no_repo_plugins has no shape assertion. Separately, main's suppression of the orphan advisory under --json is untested; a regression there would corrupt every --json consumer's stdout/stderr split silently.
drifted += record["state"] != "ok" adds a bool to an int. Correct, but arithmetic on a truth value reads as a typo, and it is the one place where the counter driving the exit code is set.

Docstring became false in the same diff that wrote it: 'Nothing in this repo reads or writes them' - find_orphan_markers, twelve lines below, reads them. Repeated at check_plugin_cache_sync.py and in docs/guide.md.

(a) find_orphan_markers rglobs the ENTIRE cache root including the plugins/ mirror the check does not compare - on Windows that is a real copy, so all 14 plugin trees get walked a second time. (b) compare_tree's not_in_cache branch hashes the whole repo tree BEFORE discovering the cache side is absent; the old code short-circuited.

Claim under doubt: a green from this gate means the shared/ tree was verified — TRACKED_SUFFIXES was a seven-suffix allowlist, so .template and extensionless files were invisible. Measured on the live cache: 44 of 1005 shared/ files unverified — shared/templates/ 3/37, shared/prompts/{code,pr,iterate}_reviewer/ 0/6. Both are read FROM THE CACHE at runtime (step-7-scaffolding.md loads templates/rules/*.md.template; external_review_prompts._DEFAULT_PROMPTS_ROOT resolves cache/shipwright/shared/prompts/). Either directory could vanish entirely under a green, and external_review_prompts._load falls back to ('', '') silently.

Claim under doubt: the gate's definition of a tree matches update-marketplace.sh's — SKIP_DIRS matched the bare component `build`, so all 29 git-tracked files of plugins/shipwright-build/skills/build/ — SKILL.md and the whole references/ tree — were dropped from BOTH sides and could never drift. Measured: 0 of 29 walked. The diff's own comment vouched for this as safe build output.

Claim under doubt: measured after: zero false positives — That measurement was taken in the clean worktree. The main checkout carries six gitignored generated files inside the compared trees (shared/.coverage, shared/.shipwright_toolcall_count, plugins/shipwright-iterate/.coverage, and three more counters). The cache is synced from a git reset --hard clone and can never hold them, so the exclusion walk made each a permanent phantom missing-from-cache: five trees drifted, --strict exit 1, and the printed remedy could not clear one of them. The mandatory --strict run would have been permanently red.

Claim under doubt: a zero-file basis can no longer render as agreement — `git ls-files` exits 0 and prints nothing when the path is inside a repo tracking nothing there (git init on an unzipped download; a copy of plugins/ inside an unrelated checkout). Treated as success it returns an empty dict, compare_tree computes no diffs, and the record is `ok` at --strict exit 0 — the same confident-green-over-nothing as the unreadable plugins/ dir, and a regression the walk basis could not produce.

Claim under doubt: the same rule is applied at both places a zero can enter — The guard sat at the LISTING step only. If git lists 1005 files and none hash (offline cloud placeholders, a disconnected mount, an AV quarantine, an all-gitlink tree), repo_tracked_files returns ({}, 'git', 1005) and compare_tree agrees with everything: ok, --strict exit 0.

Claim under doubt: verified is unaffected because the record is not ok — True for plugins, false for shared: round 3's guard was written on the plugins side only, and round 5 added a second `unreadable` producer on the unguarded shared path. So on the exact scenario the new guard was built for, the payload still said verified: ['plugins','shared'] while the shared record said no basis was established.

Claim under doubt: the OK line was fixed so it no longer overclaims — The prose was fixed; the machine-readable verdict was not. `status: ok` reads the same whether shared/ was compared or skipped as n/a, and --strict keys only on status, so every non-human consumer got the pre-fix guarantee. Separately _repo_plugin_dirs swallowed OSError into [], so an unlistable plugins/ printed 'ok - 0 plugin(s) in sync' at exit 0.

Claim under doubt: cache-only files are deliberately not drift, and that is harmless — compare_tree iterated repo-side keys only, so a DELETION never surfaced. shared/scripts is on sys.path at runtime, so a module dropped from the repo but surviving in the cache is still importable and still executes. This repo has five verifier modules devoted to catching removed code; the cache gate was blind to exactly that class.

Claim under doubt: the orphan advisory warns about what matters — Measured always-on: all 8 top-level subdirs of a fully intact cached shared/ carried a marker, re-written by a recurring sweep after each re-sync removed them, because the marker means 'not recognised as an installed plugin' — permanently true of shared/. It is not a reap prediction. And it added no detection power the tree comparison now has, since a partial reap IS drift.

Claim under doubt: the involuntary fallback is no longer silent — print_ok named it, but an involuntary fallback's characteristic outcome is DRIFT, not ok. On a safe.directory refusal the repo side reverts to walking, the gitignored files reappear as phantom drift, and the operator reads a remedy — re-run update-marketplace.sh — that cannot put .coverage into a cache. The visibility fix landed on the branch where the fallback is least likely and was absent from the branch where it produces the misdiagnosis it was written to prevent.

Claim under doubt: the documentation matches the shipped mechanism — docs/guide.md was untouched in rounds 3 and 4, so it still documented the v5 exclusion walk for BOTH sides. Its central sentence was false for the half that changed, and a reader following it would predict shared/.coverage gets compared and the run goes red — the opposite of what the code now does. Four smaller staleness items alongside. This is the iterate's own defect class: a document claiming a mechanism the code does not use.

Claim under doubt: SKIP_DIRS is safe because nothing tracked lives under those names — Correct today, but structural: before the switch both sides used the same rule, so a SKIP_DIRS name could only cause a symmetric blind spot. Now the repo side asks git and the cache side applies SKIP_DIRS, so if anything under those components ever becomes tracked it is permanent unclearable drift — the H2 failure mode with the sign flipped. The invariant was enforced by a comment.

Claim under doubt: three of the four weak-assertion fixes were made — They were not in the diff. Reported as fixed while the artifact still contained the original assertions — the same claiming-coverage-you-do-not-have failure one level up, on a change whose subject is exactly that.

Claim under doubt: the extraction is behaviour-preserving, proven by a 1,521-file differential test — The differential covered walk_tracked_files and version_key only. It could not see that latest_cache_version_dir gained a try/except the original lacked (turning an unreadable cached plugin into a confident not_in_cache with a fabricated missing-file count), nor the deliberate sample sort change.

Claim under doubt: content-sniffing is a strict improvement — It is, but the NUL heuristic is a false-GREEN risk: a binary file with no NUL in its first 8 KiB gets CRLF normalization applied before hashing, which is lossy, so two distinct blobs can hash equal.

Claim under doubt: tracked-but-unhashable files can be safely dropped — Under the walk there was no expectation to violate. Under git there is: git states how many files should be there, so dropping them shrinks tracked_count to match and a partial checkout self-consistently reports ok over a partial basis. Also hides submodule gitlinks, which hash to None.

Claim under doubt: the test suite exercises the shipped behaviour — Only the basis tests called git init; every other test ran on a non-git tmp_path, so the production basis was covered by three tests while the iterate's substantive behaviours were pinned against the basis production never uses.

Claim under doubt: every return carries the full documented shape — basis and cache_only_count were absent from _shared_na() and from the unreadable plugin record, so a consumer asserting on shared['basis'] — the key added so a consumer could tell how the verdict was established — would KeyError on four statuses.

Claim under doubt: the APPEND-not-insert(0) reasoning protects the host process — Half the mechanism was wrong: both scripts/hooks/ and shared/scripts/hooks/ lack __init__.py, so both are namespace-package PORTIONS, and a portion cannot shadow another portion — Python unions them. Only the top-level module names could shadow.

Claim under doubt: the two test files were split cleanly — _write and _seed were duplicated verbatim across two files in the same pytest root — the split traded a length rule for a duplication, and the second file's _seed docstring described the first file's concern.

external_code.disposition: Phase Matrix: External LLM Review is 'skip' at small complexity. Escalation ladder not triggered - the internal cascade ran in full (spec-reviewer PASS after two rejects, code-reviewer, doubt-reviewer), so the mandatory-external fallback for a declined cascade does not apply.
